name: secrets
description: Credential material. A match here is classified 'restricted', the highest sensitivity, and by default the egress policy refuses to send it to any cloud backend at all.

rules.name: private_key_block
rules.description: PEM private key block (RSA, EC, OPENSSH, PGP)

rules.name: private_key_header
rules.description: PEM private key header with no matching footer in this payload

rules.name: aws_secret_access_key
rules.description: AWS secret access key in key=value form

rules.name: github_token
rules.description: GitHub personal access / OAuth / server token

rules.name: llm_provider_key
rules.description: OpenAI / Anthropic style API key. PhiGate itself proxies these, so leaking one through a prompt is a direct compromise of the gateway's own upstream account.

rules.name: azure_account_key
rules.description: Azure Storage account key inside a connection string

rules.name: jwt
rules.description: JSON Web Token. The payload is only base64, so a JWT in a prompt discloses every claim it carries.

rules.name: url_credentials
rules.description: password embedded in a connection URL, e.g. postgres://user:pw@host

rules.name: generic_kv_secret
rules.description: credential in key=value or key: value form. The plausible_secret validator drops placeholders like 'changeme' and '${VAR}' so the dictionary is not polluted.
